title: Auditing Government Exams: Did India's public exams run flawlessly or get disrupted?
summary: Did India's government exams happen on time and flawlessly — or get delayed, postponed, rescheduled, or cancelled after students sat them? Audits 1,000 SHA-256-pinned Union, State, and UT government examinations across all 36 States & UTs over the past 3 years (Nov 2023 – Nov 2026) — measuring cancellations after conduct, postponements, reschedulings, delays, pre-exam cancellations, technical glitches/partial re-exams, and verified flawless-conduct benchmarks.
authority: NTA, UPSC, SSC, RRB, IBPS, CBSE, Union Ministries, State PSCs, Police/Subordinate Boards & UT Recruitment Authorities
statutory_anchors: Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024
Constitution of India Articles 315–323 (Union & State Public Service Commissions)
Official Examination Calendars, Public Notices & Digital Sansad Parliamentary Records (2023–2026)
RTI Act 2005 Sec 4(1)(b) & Sec 6(1) (Proactive Disclosure & Public Record Access)
scope: 1,000 real, SHA-256-pinned Indian public examination conduct checks (Nov 2023 – Nov 2026) across Union of India (347 tasks) and all 36 States & UTs (586 State + 67 UT tasks)
Covers 716 unique examinations across 163 conducting authorities and 858 unique live-verified official documents
Measures took-exam-then-cancelled, postponed, rescheduled, delayed, cancelled-before-conduct, and technical-glitch/partial-re-exam disruptions
Includes 262 verified flawless-conduct benchmark examinations published as Cleared with equal standing
out_of_scope: Private coaching tests, non-government university internal assessments, or unverified social media claims lacking official notices or Parliamentary records
Dynamic non-byte-stable web pages whose cryptographic SHA-256 drifts across live fetches
Personal candidate roll numbers, names, Aadhaar, PAN, phone numbers, or personal emails (scrubbed per DPDP Act 2023)
